title: CI/CD for Containers and ACR
description: Build container images, push to Azure Container Registry, and deploy to Azure Container Apps or AKS.

data.text: Container-based deployments require a slightly different CI/CD flow. Instead of deploying code directly, you build a container image, push it to a registry, and then update the running service to use the new image.

data.caption: Container CI/CD pipeline flow
data.definition:
flowchart TB
    C[Code Commit] --> B[Build Image]
    B --> P[Push to ACR]
    P --> D[Deploy to Container Apps / AKS]
    D --> V[Verify Health]
    V -->|Fail| R[Rollback]
    style B fill:#e3f2fd,stroke:#333
    style D fill:#c8e6c9,stroke:#333
    style R fill:#ffcdd2,stroke:#333

data.title: Dockerfile - .NET Web App Container
data.code:
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:8.0 AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY ["MyApp.csproj", "./"]
RUN dotnet restore
COPY . .
RUN dotnet publish -c Release -o /app/publish

FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:8.0 AS runtime
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /app/publish .
EXPOSE 8080
ENV ASPNETCORE_URLS=http://+:8080
ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "MyApp.dll"]

data.title: YAML - GitHub Actions: Build and Push to ACR
data.content: Build a container image and push to Azure Container Registry.
data.code:
name: Build and Push to ACR

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          client-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
          tenant-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
          subscription-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
          federated-credential-parameters: |
            audience: api://AzureADTokenExchange
            issuer: https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com/${{ github.repository_id }}
            subject: repo:myorg/myapp:ref:refs/heads/main
      - name: Login to ACR
        uses: azure/docker-login@v2
        with:
          login-server: myregistry.azurecr.io
      - name: Build and push
        run: |
          docker build -t myregistry.azurecr.io/myapp:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker push myregistry.azurecr.io/myapp:${{ github.sha }}

data.title: Azure CLI - Deploy Container to Container Apps
data.content: Deploy a new revision of a Container App from ACR.
data.code:
az acr login --name myregistry
docker build -t myregistry.azurecr.io/myapp:latest .
docker push myregistry.azurecr.io/myapp:latest
az containerapp update --name my-container-app --resource-group MyResourceGroup --image myregistry.azurecr.io/myapp:latest

# Or create from scratch
az containerapp create --name my-container-app --resource-group MyResourceGroup --image myregistry.azurecr.io/myapp:latest --environment my-env --ingress external --target-port 8080 --cpu 0.5 --memory 1.0Gi

data.title: Use Git Tags for Versions
data.text: Tag your container images with the Git commit SHA (github.sha) so you can always trace a deployed image back to the exact code version. Use semantic version tags for release branches.

terms.definition: A managed Docker registry service for storing and managing container images. Supports geo-replication, content trust, and Helm charts.
A specific version of a Container App container image and configuration. Container Apps support multiple revisions for safe rollouts.
The azure/docker-login GitHub Action that authenticates Docker to an Azure Container Registry using a managed identity.

data.description: Create a CI/CD pipeline for a containerized app.

Add a GitHub Actions workflow that builds and pushes the image
Create an Azure Container App environment
Deploy the Container App using the image from ACR
Browse to the Container App URL and confirm it works
data.expectedOutcome: A containerized web app deployed to Azure Container Apps, built and pushed via CI/CD.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Container CI/CD builds an image, pushes to a registry, then deploys
Use ACR as your private container registry in Azure
Tag images with the Git SHA for traceability
Azure Container Apps and AKS both support rolling updates from new images
data.takeaway: Container deployments require a registry (ACR) and a runtime (Container Apps or AKS). Automate the full image build-and-deploy cycle.
